extracted.intended_audience: NLP researchers and practitioners generating or evaluating text datasets with large language models
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and empirical findings about generating diverse, high-quality text datasets using large language models and human interventions (label correction and filtering). Focus is on balancing diversity and label/text accuracy for downstream model training and evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure of how varied the generated text is (lexical/linguistic variety, coverage of classes/languages/topics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper examines approaches to diversify text generation (logit suppression and temperature sampling). Diversification approaches can increase data diversity but often at the cost of data accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data accuracy (text and labels appropriate for target domain)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the generated text and their associated labels are correct and appropriate for the intended target domain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors define accuracy as 'text and labels being appropriate for the target domain' and note that diversification often reduces this accuracy. Improvements (e.g., label replacement) can increase absolute accuracy (reported +14.4% in oracle studies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Logit suppression (diversification technique)
rubrics_metrics.description: A generation technique that minimizes the generation of languages that have already been frequently generated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as an approach to diversify output by suppressing over-represented generation; trade-offs include potential reduction in data accuracy when applied without human intervention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temperature sampling (diversification technique)
rubrics_metrics.description: A generation technique that flattens the token sampling probability to encourage more varied outputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to increase diversity by making less-probable tokens more likely; similarly can increase diversity at the expense of accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Label replacement (LR) — human intervention
rubrics_metrics.description: Human correction of misaligned or incorrect labels assigned to generated instances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LR is evaluated in oracle studies and found to increase the absolute accuracy of models trained with diversified datasets by 14.4%. Some models trained on LR-processed generated data outperformed LLM-based few-shot classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Out-of-scope filtering (OOSF) — human intervention
rubrics_metrics.description: Human removal of generated instances that are out of the user's domain of interest or to which no considered label applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OOSF was evaluated and found not effective in increasing downstream model accuracy according to the paper, suggesting need for further research on filtering strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trade-off: diversity versus accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: The inherent tension where methods that increase diversity can decrease accuracy of text and labels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper explicitly notes that diversification approaches can increase data diversity but often at the cost of data accuracy, motivating the use of human interventions to recover accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation via oracle studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of oracle/controlled human-in-the-loop experiments to measure the effects of diversification techniques and interventions on dataset quality and downstream performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oracle studies are used to quantify the impact of interventions (e.g., LR increases absolute accuracy by 14.4%). This implies a recommended evaluation practice: measure interventions' effects concretely using controlled evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Downstream model performance as a quality metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessing the usefulness of generated data by training models on it and measuring their performance (including comparisons to LLM-based few-shot classification).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper reports that some models trained with LR-augmented generated data outperformed LLM-based few-shot classification, indicating downstream task performance is a primary practical criterion for dataset quality.
